literal: Emperor Zhuang posthumously restored the princely title, posthumously Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhongwu.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang restored his princely rank, posthumously made him Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhongwu.

literal: Zhan's younger brother Jin, Director of the Masters of Writing in the Sacrifices Section.
idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Jin was director of sacrifices in the Masters of Writing.

literal: Later plotted to kill Qi Emperor Wenxiang.
idiomatic: Later he plotted to kill Emperor Wenxiang of Qi.

literal: The affair leaked; the whole household suffered execution by law.
idiomatic: The plot failed; the whole clan was executed.

literal: Zhan's son Falun was born to Ziguang.
idiomatic: Zhan's son Falun was born to Lady Ziguang.

literal: The Qi king pitied Zhan's extinction and then memorialized to restore him, restoring his title and lands.
idiomatic: The Qi emperor pitied Zhan's fall and restored Falun's title and lands.

literal: Prince of Nan'an Yu, in Zhenjun year three enfeoffed Prince of Wu, later changed to Prince of Nan'an.
idiomatic: Yu, Prince of Nan'an, was enfeoffed Prince of Wu in Zhenjun year three, later Prince of Nan'an.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu suddenly collapsed, Palace Attendant Zong Ai forged the empress dowager's order to welcome and establish him, then afterward issued mourning.
idiomatic: When Taiwu died suddenly, Zong Ai forged the empress dowager's order, enthroned Yu, then announced mourning.

literal: Great amnesty, changed the era to Yongping.
idiomatic: He declared a great amnesty and the era Yongping.

literal: Yu himself because he was established out of order, richly gifted the ranks below, taking pleasure from the multitude.
idiomatic: Knowing his accession irregular, Yu lavished gifts on the court to win favor.

literal: Made long-night drinking; music and sound unceasing.
idiomatic: He held endless night feasts; music never stopped.

literal: Within a ten-day month the treasury was emptied.
idiomatic: Within a month the treasury was bare.

literal: He especially loved falconry and hunting, going out without measure.
idiomatic: He loved hunting beyond measure.

literal: The frontier reported hardship; Yu did not pity it; the hundred surnames were angry and grieved, yet Yu was serene.
idiomatic: The frontier cried for help; Yu ignored it; the people raged while he remained serene.

literal: Zong Ai's power grew daily; inside and outside feared him.
idiomatic: Zong Ai's power grew daily; court and realm feared him.

literal: Yu suspected Ai would change and plotted to seize his power.
idiomatic: Yu suspected Ai's treachery and plotted to seize his power.

literal: Ai because Yu sacrificed at the temple killed Yu at night.
idiomatic: Ai killed Yu on a night of ancestral sacrifice.

literal: Emperor Wencheng buried him with princely rites, posthumous name Yin.
idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng buried him with princely rites, posthumous name Yin.

literal: Discussion says: The owl and jackal as creatures—heaven truly bore them.
idiomatic: The commentators say: Owls and jackals are creatures heaven itself begets.

literal: Observing what Yuan Shao harbored, he also especially received perverse qi.
idiomatic: Yuan Shao's heart, they say, was specially steeped in foul breath.

literal: From Pingyang down, all many early deaths;
idiomatic: From Pingyang downward, princes died young;

literal: talent and martial stratagem did not show in advanced years.
idiomatic: talent and arms rarely reached old age.

literal: Princes Jing and Jian, for the time were called foremost.
idiomatic: Princes Jing and Jian were the age's foremost.

literal: Jian already had reputation; Hun also was regarded as vessel.
idiomatic: Jian won renown; Hun was esteemed as well.

literal: Xiao and Ji bore favor in Taihe's days—name and rank, could they be reached in vain!
idiomatic: Xiao and Ji flourished under Taihe—who could match their rank lightly?

literal: Cha climbed by favor and private ties, then disordered the realm; killing the body yet preserving sacrifice—indeed fortunate.
idiomatic: Cha rose by favor and wrecked the realm; to die yet keep his rites was fortune enough.

literal: Princes of Leping and Le'an both by general's merit served effect; in the end because of anxious pressure they passed—proof that completing the end is rare.
idiomatic: Leping and Le'an served as generals yet died under strain—few finish the course.

literal: Prince Zhuang's talent, strength, wisdom, and stratagem—a hero of the time; with Princes of Jianning and Xinxing, not the same day.
idiomatic: Prince Zhuang's wit was a hero of his day, unlike Jianning and Xinxing.

literal: Among Taiwu's sons, Qin and Jin were talented.
idiomatic: Among Taiwu's sons, Qin and Jin showed talent.

literal: Yet Han's meeting with cruelty—how can fortune and misfortune be measured!
idiomatic: Yet Han met cruelty—who can measure fortune's turn?

literal: After Huaiyang, Yu was abundant virtue;
idiomatic: After Huaiyang, Yu bore abundant virtue;

literal: In Guangyang's generation Jia was truly beautiful; Shen's faults toward Yuan Hui—the so-called thief hates righteousness.
idiomatic: Guangyang's Jia was fair; Shen's evil toward Yuan Hui was the thief hating the just.

literal: Zuo being seen killed—not a late foundation!
idiomatic: That Zuo was slain was no late ruin!
